Each excerpt includes the instruction files found in the log (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md). For Claude Code sessions without them, the current CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and AGENTS.md files of the project folder and your global CLAUDE.md are added (--no-current-instructions turns this off).

  Estimated total $2.57 at API list prices, billed to whatever account the CLI is logged in with (plan quota on a subscription, money on an API key)
  These are upper estimates for the input: nothing is assumed to come from the provider's prompt cache. Judging the same sessions again soon after costs less, because the cache is reused.
Grouping by meaning after judging: Claude Code on, Codex on. Turn a tool off or on with --grouping claude=off (or settings.json "grouping").
After judging, 2 grouping call(s) (Claude Code, Codex), about $0.14 in total: each provider gets only its own sessions' judged problems (the quotes and summaries the judge already saw) and groups them by meaning. --no-grouping skips this.
Privacy: logs, cache and reports stay on this computer. Two things go out: the drift check sends each selected session to its own provider's official CLI (claude -p or codex exec), which sends it wherever that CLI is set up to (its logged-in account, or a base URL or proxy you configured) together with the CLI's own telemetry, and then makes one grouping call per provider with that provider's judged problems (the same quotes the judge already saw, plus its summaries; --no-grouping skips it); and `self-update --check` asks GitHub for the latest release tag. Nothing else opens a network connection (`privacy` lists the details).
--dry-run: estimate only, nothing judged.
To judge fewer or other sessions: --max-sessions N (how many, most recent first), --since 7d (the period), --project <name> (one project).
